q: What is the capital of Australia?
x: Canberra was purpose-built as a compromise between rivals Sydney and Melbourne; Parliament first sat there in 1927.

q: What is the capital of Canada?
x: Queen Victoria chose Ottawa as the capital in 1857. Toronto is Canada's largest city.

q: What is the capital of Japan?
x: Kyoto was the imperial capital for over a thousand years; the emperor moved to Tokyo (then called Edo) in 1868-69.

q: What is the capital of Spain?
x: Madrid sits close to the geographical centre of the Iberian Peninsula.

q: What is the capital of Italy?
x: Rome became the capital of a unified Italy in 1871. Turin and then Florence held the title before it.

q: What is the capital of Germany?
x: Bonn was West Germany's capital. Berlin became the capital of reunified Germany in 1990, and the government moved there in 1999.

q: What is the capital of Brazil?
x: Brasília was built from scratch in the country's interior and replaced Rio de Janeiro as capital in 1960.

q: What is the capital of Turkey?
x: Atatürk made Ankara the capital of the new republic in 1923. Istanbul is still by far the largest city.

q: What is the capital of New Zealand?
x: Wellington has been the capital since 1865 and is the southernmost capital city of any sovereign state.

q: Which city is the seat of Switzerland's federal government?
x: The Swiss constitution names no capital: Bern is officially the 'federal city'. Zurich is the largest city.

q: What is the capital of Morocco?
x: Rabat is on the Atlantic coast; Casablanca, a little further south, is the largest city.

q: What is the capital of Vietnam?
x: Hanoi is in the north. Ho Chi Minh City in the south, formerly Saigon, has more people.

q: What is the capital of Pakistan?
x: Islamabad was built in the 1960s as a planned capital, taking over from Karachi, which is still the largest city.

q: What is the capital of Iceland?
x: Reykjavík is the northernmost capital city of any sovereign state.

q: What is the capital of South Korea?
x: About half of South Korea's people live in the Seoul metropolitan area.

q: What is the capital of Kazakhstan?
x: The capital moved from Almaty to Astana in 1997. The city was renamed Nur-Sultan in 2019 and went back to Astana in 2022.

q: What is the capital of Nigeria?
x: Abuja, a planned city in the centre of the country, replaced Lagos as the capital in 1991.

q: What is the capital of Mongolia?
x: Ulaanbaatar is often called the coldest capital city in the world: its average yearly temperature is below freezing.

q: What is the official capital of Tanzania?
x: Dodoma is the official capital and home of the National Assembly; Dar es Salaam is the largest city and main port.

q: What is the official capital of Côte d'Ivoire (Ivory Coast)?
x: Yamoussoukro has been the official capital since 1983, but Abidjan is the largest city and economic centre.

q: Which city replaced Yangon as the capital of Myanmar in the 2000s?
x: The government moved to the purpose-built city of Naypyidaw in 2005-06. Yangon is still the largest city.

q: Which country's flag has a red maple leaf in the middle?
x: The Maple Leaf flag was adopted in 1965, replacing the Canadian Red Ensign.

q: Which country's flag is a red circle on a plain white background?
x: Japan's flag is called the Hinomaru, 'circle of the sun'. Bangladesh also has a red disc, but on green.

q: Which country's national flag is nicknamed the Union Jack?
x: The Union Flag combines the crosses of St George (England), St Andrew (Scotland) and St Patrick (Ireland).

q: How many stars are on the flag of the United States?
x: One star for each state; the 13 stripes stand for the original 13 colonies. The 50-star version dates from 1960.

q: Which three colours make up the flag of Italy?
x: Italians call it il Tricolore: three vertical bands, green at the hoist. Green, white and orange is Ireland.

q: Which country's flag has a blue globe and a band of stars inside a yellow diamond on green?
x: The banner across the globe reads 'Ordem e Progresso' (Order and Progress). Its 27 stars stand for the states and the Federal District.

q: Which country has a square national flag with a white cross on red?
x: Switzerland and Vatican City are the only countries with square national flags. Denmark's white cross on red is rectangular and off-centre.

q: Which tree appears on the flag of Lebanon?
x: A green Lebanon cedar sits on a white band between two red bands.

q: What is shown in the middle of India's flag?
x: The navy-blue Ashoka Chakra, a wheel with 24 spokes, sits on the white band between saffron and green.

q: Which country's flag is a yellow cross on a blue background?
x: Finland has a blue cross on white, Norway a blue-and-white cross on red, Denmark a white cross on red.

q: Which country's flag shows an eagle eating a snake while perched on a cactus?
x: It recalls the Aztec legend of where to found their capital, Tenochtitlan, on the site of today's Mexico City.

q: Which country's flag is red with a white crescent and a white star?
x: Pakistan's crescent and star are white on green; Algeria's crescent is red; Malaysia's is yellow on blue.

q: Which country's flag has a white cross on red that is set towards the hoist side?
x: The Dannebrog is often said to be the oldest national flag still in use. Its off-centre 'Nordic cross' was copied by its neighbours.

q: Which country's flag has a black, gold and green diagonal cross?
x: Jamaica adopted the flag, with its gold saltire, at independence in 1962.

q: Which country's national flag is not a rectangle or a square, but two stacked triangles?
x: Nepal's flag is made of two pennants, one above the other, with a white moon and sun.

q: Which country's flag shows a white dragon?
x: Bhutan's name for itself, Druk Yul, means 'Land of the Thunder Dragon', and the Druk appears on its flag.

q: Which country's flag includes an AK-47 rifle?
x: The rifle is crossed with a hoe on top of an open book. Angola's flag has a half cogwheel and a machete.

q: Which country's flag carries a red-and-white chequered shield?
x: The chequerboard (šahovnica) sits in the middle of a red, white and blue tricolour.

q: Which country's flag has 14 red and white stripes?
x: The 14 stripes stand for the 13 states and the federal government. The US flag has 13 stripes, Liberia's 11.

q: Which country's flag has a broken trident in the middle?
x: The trident of Neptune, with its shaft broken off, stands for the island's break from colonial rule at independence in 1966.

q: Which country's flag shows a purple-and-green Sisserou parrot?
x: The Sisserou is Dominica's national bird and is found nowhere else in the world.

q: Which is the largest ocean?
x: The Pacific covers about a third of Earth's surface, more than all the land put together.

q: On which continent is the Sahara Desert?
x: The Sahara is the largest hot desert in the world, stretching across much of North Africa.

q: Which is the highest mountain above sea level?
x: A joint China-Nepal survey in 2020 put Everest's height at 8,849 m.

q: Which river flows through London?
x: The Thames is about 346 km long. The Severn is the UK's longest river.

q: Which is the smallest continent by land area?
x: Australia covers about 7.7 million km². Europe is the second smallest.

q: On which continent is the Amazon rainforest?
x: Most of it is in Brazil, with the rest in eight other countries and territories.

q: The Strait of Gibraltar links the Atlantic Ocean to which sea?
x: At its narrowest, the strait between Spain and Morocco is less than 15 km wide.

q: Which is the longest river in Europe?
x: The Volga runs for about 3,500 km through Russia and empties into the Caspian Sea.

q: Which is the deepest lake in the world?
x: Baikal in Siberia is over 1,600 m deep and holds roughly a fifth of the world's unfrozen surface fresh water.

q: Which mountain range in Russia is usually taken as part of the boundary between Europe and Asia?
x: The Urals run roughly north to south for about 2,500 km, from the Arctic towards Kazakhstan.

q: Which two countries share the longest international border in the world?
x: Including Alaska's border with Canada, it runs for about 8,900 km. Russia and Kazakhstan share the second longest.

q: Not counting Australia, which is the largest island in the world?
x: Greenland covers about 2.2 million km². It is an autonomous territory within the Kingdom of Denmark.

q: Which river carries the most water into the sea?
x: The Amazon delivers roughly a fifth of all the river water that flows into the world's oceans.

q: Which country lies entirely inside South Africa?
x: Only three countries are completely surrounded by another one: Lesotho, and San Marino and Vatican City inside Italy.

q: Victoria Falls is on which river?
x: The falls are on the border between Zambia and Zimbabwe. The local name, Mosi-oa-Tunya, means 'the smoke that thunders'.

q: Mount Kilimanjaro, Africa's highest mountain, is in which country?
x: Kilimanjaro is a dormant volcano close to the Kenyan border, 5,895 m high.

q: Which is the longest mountain range on land?
x: The Andes run about 7,000 km down the western side of South America, through seven countries.

q: The shore of which body of water is the lowest point on land?
x: The Dead Sea shore is more than 400 m below sea level, and the water level is still falling.

q: The Atacama, one of the driest places on Earth, is mostly in which country?
x: Some weather stations in the Atacama have never recorded rain.

q: Which is the only sea with no land coastline?
x: The Sargasso Sea in the North Atlantic is bounded by ocean currents rather than land, and is named after its floating sargassum seaweed.

q: Counting its overseas territories, which country spans the most time zones?
x: Thanks to territories from French Polynesia to Réunion, France spans 12 time zones; Russia, on its own landmass, has 11.

q: Which country has the longest coastline in the world?
x: Canada's mainland and its thousands of Arctic islands give it a coastline of over 200,000 km.

q: Which country is often said to hold more than half of the world's lakes?
x: Canada has hundreds of thousands of lakes, many of them scooped out by glaciers during the last ice age.

q: Counting cold deserts, which is the largest desert on Earth?
x: A desert is defined by how little rain or snow falls, not by heat, and Antarctica gets very little of either.

q: Which is the largest country in the world by area?
x: Russia covers about 17.1 million km², roughly 11% of the world's land.

q: According to UN estimates, which country has had the most people since 2023?
x: The UN estimates India passed China during 2023. As of 2024 both have about 1.4 billion people.

q: Which is the smallest country in the world by area?
x: Vatican City covers less than half a square kilometre, entirely inside Rome.

q: Which is the largest country in South America by area?
x: Brazil covers nearly half of South America and borders every country on the continent except Chile and Ecuador.

q: Which continent has the most people?
x: About 60% of the world's people live in Asia.

q: Roughly how much of Earth's surface is covered by water?
x: Almost all of it is ocean; fresh water is only a small share of the total.

q: Which country has the most people in Africa?
x: As of 2024 Nigeria has over 220 million people; Ethiopia is second.

q: Which is the largest country in Africa by area?
x: Sudan was the largest until South Sudan became independent in 2011; since then it has been Algeria.

q: Which is the second-largest country in the world by area?
x: Canada covers about 10 million km², a little more than the United States or China.

q: Which country in the European Union has the most people?
x: As of 2024 Germany has about 84 million people, France about 68 million.

q: In which year did the world's population reach 8 billion, according to the UN?
x: The UN marked 15 November 2022 as the 'Day of Eight Billion'. The 7 billion mark was in 2011.

q: Which is the largest US state by area?
x: Alaska is more than twice the size of Texas, the second largest.

q: Which US state has the most people?
x: As of 2024 California has about 39 million people, Texas about 31 million.

q: Which country, made up entirely of islands, has the most people?
x: As of 2024 Indonesia has about 280 million people, spread over more than 17,000 islands.

q: Which is the largest country in the European Union by area?
x: Even without its overseas regions, France (about 550,000 km²) is bigger than second-placed Spain (about 506,000 km²).

q: According to UN estimates, which country has the third-largest population (as of 2024)?
x: About 340 million people, behind India and China. Indonesia is fourth.

q: Which is the largest lake in the world by surface area?
x: The salty Caspian covers about 370,000 km². Lake Superior is the largest freshwater lake by area.

q: Which is the largest landlocked country?
x: Kazakhstan covers about 2.7 million km², making it the ninth-largest country of all.

q: Which country is the most densely populated?
x: Monaco squeezes about 38,000 residents into around 2 km². Singapore leads among countries over 1 million people.

q: About how many people live in Greenland (as of 2024)?
x: The world's largest island has around 57,000 inhabitants, about a third of them in the capital, Nuuk.

q: Which is the largest country lying entirely in the Southern Hemisphere?
x: Brazil is bigger, but the equator crosses its north, so part of it is in the Northern Hemisphere.

q: In which city is the Colosseum?
x: The amphitheatre was finished in AD 80 and could hold tens of thousands of spectators.

q: In which country is Machu Picchu?
x: The Inca citadel was built in the 15th century high in the Andes, above the Urubamba valley.

q: Which city is overlooked by the Christ the Redeemer statue?
x: The statue was completed in 1931 on top of Corcovado mountain.

q: The Statue of Liberty was a gift to the United States from which country?
x: It was dedicated in New York Harbor in 1886. Gustave Eiffel's company engineered its inner frame.

q: In which city is the Sagrada Família?
x: Antoni Gaudí took charge of the basilica in 1883 and worked on it until his death in 1926.

q: In which city is the Brandenburg Gate?
x: The gate was completed in 1791. It stood just inside East Berlin while the Wall divided the city.

q: Which city is the Golden Gate Bridge in?
x: When it opened in 1937 it was the longest suspension bridge span in the world. Its colour is called International Orange.

q: The Eiffel Tower was built for which event?
w: The end of the First World War
x: It was the entrance arch to the 1889 Exposition Universelle and was meant to stand for only 20 years.

q: In which city is the Taj Mahal?
x: The Mughal emperor Shah Jahan built it as a tomb for his wife Mumtaz Mahal.

q: In which country is the ancient city of Petra?
x: The Nabataeans carved Petra's buildings straight into rose-coloured sandstone cliffs.

q: In which country is Angkor Wat?
x: Built in the 12th century, it is one of the largest religious monuments in the world, and it appears on Cambodia's flag.

q: Which of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World is still standing?
x: It is also the oldest of the seven, built around 4,500 years ago, and was the tallest human-made structure for over 3,800 years.

q: Stonehenge is in which English county?
x: It stands on Salisbury Plain. Its first stage was built around 5,000 years ago.

q: As of 2025, which is the tallest building in the world?
x: The Dubai tower is 828 m tall and has held the record since it opened in 2010.

q: In which country is Neuschwanstein Castle?
x: King Ludwig II of Bavaria had it built from 1869. It is said to have inspired Disney's Sleeping Beauty castle.

q: Which city is home to the Hagia Sophia?
x: It was completed in 537 under the Byzantine emperor Justinian, and its dome was the largest in the world for centuries.

q: The giant stone Moai figures are on which island?
x: The island, called Rapa Nui by its people, is part of Chile, about 3,500 km off its coast.

q: Chichén Itzá in Mexico was a great city of which civilisation?
x: Its step pyramid, El Castillo, has stairways on all four sides.

q: In which Spanish city is the Alhambra palace?
x: The palace and fortress complex was built mainly in the 13th and 14th centuries by the Nasrid dynasty.

q: In which country is Borobudur, the world's largest Buddhist temple?
x: It was built on the island of Java in the 9th century.

q: A 2012 Chinese survey measured all the branches of the Great Wall of China. Roughly how long did it find it to be?
x: The survey counted 21,196 km of walls, trenches and natural barriers, built over many dynasties.

q: In which country are the ruins of Persepolis, the ancient Persian capital?
x: Darius the Great began building it around 518 BC.

q: Which planet is closest to the Sun?
x: Mercury goes round the Sun once every 88 Earth days.

q: Which planet is known as the Red Planet?
x: Its red colour comes from iron oxide, essentially rust, in its dust and rocks.

q: Which is the largest planet in the Solar System?
x: Jupiter is more than twice as massive as all the other planets put together.

q: How many sides does a hexagon have?
x: Honeybees build their combs from hexagonal cells, which use the least wax for the space they enclose.

q: Who painted the Mona Lisa?
x: It hangs in the Louvre in Paris, behind protective glass.

q: Who wrote the play Romeo and Juliet?
x: It was probably written in the mid-1590s and is set in Verona.

q: Who was the first person to walk on the Moon?
x: Armstrong stepped onto the Moon during Apollo 11 in July 1969; Buzz Aldrin followed about 20 minutes later.

q: What is the chemical symbol for gold?
x: Au comes from the Latin word for gold, aurum. Ag is silver.

q: What is the hardest natural substance?
x: Diamond is pure carbon and scores 10, the top of the Mohs hardness scale.

q: Which gas makes up most of Earth's atmosphere?
x: Nitrogen is about 78% of the air and oxygen about 21%.

q: In which year did the Berlin Wall fall?
x: The border crossings opened on 9 November 1989; Germany was reunified less than a year later.

q: Which element has the atomic number 1?
x: Hydrogen is the lightest and most common element in the universe.

q: Who invented the World Wide Web?
x: He proposed it in 1989 while working at CERN, the physics laboratory near Geneva.

q: What is the smallest prime number?
x: 2 is also the only even prime. 1 doesn't count as a prime number.

q: Which language has the most native speakers?
x: Mandarin has over 900 million native speakers. English has the most speakers in total once second-language speakers are counted.

q: What is the longest bone in the human body?
x: The femur, or thigh bone, is also the strongest bone in the body.

q: Who wrote On the Origin of Species, published in 1859?
x: It set out his theory of evolution by natural selection, shaped partly by his voyage on HMS Beagle.

q: How many bones are in the adult human body?
x: Babies are born with more, around 300, and many of them fuse together as they grow.

q: Roughly how fast does light travel in a vacuum?
x: Exactly 299,792,458 metres per second. Sunlight takes about 8 minutes to reach Earth.

q: Which planet spins on its side, tilted at about 98 degrees?
x: One idea is that a huge collision long ago knocked it over.

q: As of 2025, which planet has the most known moons?
x: In 2025 astronomers announced 128 more small moons of Saturn, taking its count to 274, far ahead of Jupiter.

q: In which country were the first modern Olympic Games held, in 1896?
x: Athens hosted them, with athletes from 14 nations.
